section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: Building Dimensions
section_1.content: Briefly establish the transition from 1D (line), to 2D (circle), and 3D (sphere) using the general algebraic form: x₁² + x₂² + ... + xₙ² = r².
section_1.example: Visualize a 'Flatland' character realizing that adding a third coordinate (z) transforms a circle into a sphere.

section_2.title: Defining the N-Sphere
section_2.content: Introduce the n-sphere (Sⁿ) as the set of points at a constant distance 'r' from a center in (n+1)-dimensional space. Emphasize that the 'dimension' refers to the surface manifold.
section_2.example: A 1-sphere is the perimeter of a circle; a 2-sphere is the shell of a 3D ball; a 3-sphere is the 'surface' of a 4D hypersphere.

section_3.title: The Paradox of Volume and Surface Area
section_3.content: Explain how the volume of a unit n-ball behaves counter-intuitively as n increases—specifically, how volume concentrates near the 'equator' and eventually tends to zero as n goes to infinity.
section_3.example: Imagine an orange in 100-dimensional space: almost all its 'fruit' (volume) is concentrated in a thin layer just beneath the 'peel' (surface).

section_4.title: Visualizing the Un-visualizable
section_4.content: Use orthogonal projection techniques to demonstrate how a 4D hypersphere (a Tesseract-like containment) would look if sliced through our 3D reality.
section_4.example: An animation of a 4D sphere passing through 3D space: it appears as a point, grows into a sphere, reaches maximum size, shrinks, and vanishes.

section_5.title: Applications: Data Science and Beyond
section_5.content: Connect high-dimensional geometry to modern AI, specifically how 'Curse of Dimensionality' impacts machine learning algorithms.
section_5.example: A robot learning to walk in high-dimensional state space: explain that as dimensions increase, data points become 'sparse,' making it harder for the robot to find the 'correct' movement pattern.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1
                y = 2.5 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "We build dimensions from 1D, to 2D, to 3D.",
            "The algebraic form grows with each new dimension.",
            "An n-sphere exists in n+1 dimensional space."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Building Dimensions", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        circle = Circle(radius=0.8, color="#FF5733")
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "C2")
        label1 = Text("Circle", font_size=20, color="#FF5733")
        label1.next_to(circle, UP)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(circle), Write(label1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        radius_line = Line(circle.get_center(), circle.get_right(), color="#33FF57")
        r_label = MathTex("r", color="#33FF57").next_to(radius_line, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(radius_line), Write(r_label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        sphere = Circle(radius=1.0, color="#3357FF")
